newsitem.title: USA: Eastman Kodak shares sag on flat sales.
newsitem.headline: Eastman Kodak shares sag on flat sales.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co's disclosure of flat sales in January and February confirmed analysts' suspicions and could lead some to downgrade the stock.
"We have a buy on the stock but it's a very cold buy. We will be reviewing it," said Prudential Securities analyst Alex Henderson.
Rochester, N.Y.-based Kodak's shares fell 8-1/8 to 80-1/8, or over nine percent, after the company said its January and February sales were essentially flat compared to the same period last year.
Kodak cited lower prices, a rising dollar and slower growth in emerging markets.
Henderson said Kodak's market share was declining, and a consumer shift toward mass merchandisers and wholesale shopping clubs had reduced Kodak revenues.

"Clearly, currency is a problem. There's a 10 percent negative currency translation on most multinationals. We also think Kodak is losing a substantial amount of market share, about three percent in the last few months," he said.
But analysts cautioned against wholesale dumping of the stock, noting Kodak typically shows slow growth in the first two months of the year.

"You've got inventory adjustments and all kinds of retail factors that go into it," said one analyst. "It historically has not been a critical period and is certainly not indicative of the rest of the year."
Henderson said the market's reaction to the news was a bit excessive. He said the stock could trade in the $84-$86 range.
"I think it's going to take the company four quarters to work through these issues, but my guess is at this price ($80) the stock is oversold," he said.

Kodak Chief Financial Officer Harry Kavetas said, "Although 1997 has started more slowly than we expected, there is nothing in these first months which would cause us to change our fundamental operating plans and objectives."
